[suggestion] Cycle-aware coaching for female users — wire up the ALREADY-BUILT-but-dormant menstrual-cycle scaffolding so a female user can log her cycle and the coach's existing phase logic finally fires on real data.

Feature (one sentence): An optional cycle log (last-period start date + average cycle length) that computes the current phase (menstrual / follicular / luteal) and feeds it to the AI coach, so training-load and calorie/nutrition guidance adapt to the phase — activating coach + content logic NYUS already ships but currently never receives real data for.

Problem: NYUS collects gender at onboarding (src/pages/onboarding/Screen2_BasicInfo.tsx:117-131) and already gates female-specific questions (pregnancy_status in src/lib/coach-intake-questions.ts:369-385; PCOD/PCOS flag in src/pages/onboarding/Screen5_Health.tsx:25). The backend even has the columns — menstrual_cycle_tracking + cycle_length_days (nyu_backend/db_models.py:1260-1261, migrated in scripts/apply_v4_migration.py:139) — the coach prompts ALREADY reason about follicular/luteal phases (llm_prompts.py:670,698; prompts/coach_system.txt:46,113-115; prompts/coaching_decisions.txt:120-123; prompts/science/weight_fluctuations.txt:19-23, e.g. "+100-300 kcal in luteal, expect water retention"), and cycle/PMS diet plans are already seeded (docs/diet-plans/plans/special-populations/cycle-phase-menstrual.md + pms-supportive.md via scripts/gen_90_diet_plans.py:829-859). So for ~half the user base the coach's phase intelligence is dead data — it can talk about luteal cravings in the abstract but never knows the user is actually in her luteal phase.

Evidence summary: the expensive parts (coach science, schema columns, phase-specific meal content) are built and shipping UNUSED; the only missing data point is the last-period anchor + the wiring to read it. Verified by reading each cited file.

Why now: A thin wiring layer unlocks a genuinely differentiated, on-brand coaching feature for the largest currently-underserved segment. Whoop (a stated brand reference) and HealthifyMe both ship cycle-phase training/nutrition insights; NYUS silently treats a female athlete's month as flat despite having already paid for the hard parts.

V1 scope (female users only, opt-in): (1) add ONE field — last_period_date — the single missing data point; reuse the existing dormant menstrual_cycle_tracking (opt-in toggle) + cycle_length_days columns. (2) Client-side phase = f(last_period_date, cycle_length_days) → a small calm "You're in your luteal phase" card (Dashboard / coach surface) with 1-2 concrete tips pulled from the already-seeded phase plan content. (3) Inject the current phase into the coach context string so its existing phase logic fires on real data. Explicitly OUT of v1: no predictions, no fertility/ovulation claims, no symptom tracking, no medical framing.

Effort: small-medium. BE: 1 new column (last_period_date) + a serializer exposing computed phase + read the 2 dormant columns. FE: 1 opt-in cycle-log screen + 1 phase card + trivial phase math. No new nutrition science or coach-prompt work — both already exist.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Nutrition "Food preferences" sheet never loads the user's saved preferences, so its "tap to edit" is impossible and tapping Save silently OVERWRITES (wipes) the saved food intolerances + cuisines — including allergy intolerances that drive meal generation.

Component: src/pages/_components/nutrition/NutritionPlanActions.tsx (rendered on /nutrition under "Fine-tune your plan", Nutrition.tsx:501).

What's wrong:
- The sheet's selection state is initialised EMPTY and is NEVER hydrated from the profile: intolerances=useState<string[]>([]) and cuisines=useState<string[]>([]) (NutritionPlanActions.tsx:53-54). No effect syncs profile.food_intolerances / profile.cuisine_preferences into that state — even though the component already reads those arrays for the row's count (prefsCount, :62).
- The row subtitle reads "{{count}} set — tap to edit" (en.json nutrition.plan_actions.food_prefs_set) with a green check when prefs exist (:121,:124-125), promising an editable view.
- handleSave ALWAYS sends both keys built from the (empty-started) state: food_intolerances: intolerances.map(i=>i.toLowerCase()), cuisine_preferences: cuisines.map(c=>c.toLowerCase()) (:77-80), then POSTs /profile/food-prefs.
- The backend endpoint DOES exist (the "backend endpoint pending" comment at :91 is STALE) and REPLACES each column it receives: for field,value in updates.items(): setattr(hp,field,value) (backend app/routes/profile.py:671-672); an explicit [] clears the column (documented at profile.py:611-614).
- Worse, the "Saved!" success toast fires UNCONDITIONALLY even if the POST throws — the catch only logs (:90-92) then always toasts (:93-94).

Expected: opening the sheet pre-selects the chips matching the saved intolerances/cuisines so they can be seen and edited; Save preserves anything not changed; a failed save shows an error, not "Saved!".

Actual: the sheet opens with ALL chips DESELECTED regardless of saved prefs; there is no way to view/edit the real values; tapping Save (default empty selection, or a partial one) posts arrays that overwrite/clear the saved dietary prefs server-side — and the app claims "Saved!" even when the request fails.

Repro:
1. Have saved food prefs (e.g. onboarding set intolerances Nuts+Gluten, cuisine Indian) — the /nutrition "Food preferences" row shows "3 set — tap to edit" + a check.
2. Tap the row → sheet opens with EVERY chip unselected.
3. Tap Save without re-picking → payload sends empty arrays → backend clears food_intolerances + cuisine_preferences (allergies gone) → UI shows "Saved!".

Fix: on open, seed intolerances/cuisines from profile (map stored lowercase values back to the option casing); and/or only include a key in the payload when the user actually changed it; gate the success toast on POST success.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED (full-stack) — shipped, awaiting on-device verify. Root cause was two-layer: (1) GET /profile/basic-info never serialized food_intolerances/cuisine_preferences, so the sheet had nothing to hydrate from and prefsCount was always 0; (2) the sheet state started empty, always sent both keys on Save (clearing stored prefs server-side), and toasted "Saved!" unconditionally even on POST failure. Fixes: backend backend.py adds both fields to basic-info (deployed to prod, verified LIVE: basic-info now returns food_intolerances:[nuts,gluten], cuisine_preferences:[indian] for the QA acct) [commit 0af6c3c]; frontend NutritionPlanActions.tsx now hydrates chips from the profile on sheet-open (lowercase→option casing, preserving unknown values) and gates the success toast on POST success with a destructive error toast otherwise [commit 6275a222]. tsc clean; test:unit gate green. Full-screen sheet capture not possible in the QA env: the Fine-tune hub is gated behind hasMeals and this account has no active date-covering diet plan to render it (deep provisioning prohibited per owner directive). Please verify the sheet on-device (it has a real plan) and Resolve.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] On an intermittent-fasting (16:8) day the Nutrition meal list stays blur-covered and CLICK-BLOCKED for the entire day — even after the fast completes and the banner says "Eating window open" — so the user cannot log / skip / swap / adjust any meal without turning fasting off.

Component: src/pages/Nutrition.tsx.

What's wrong:
- The blur+dark overlay over the meal list renders whenever fastingDay && fastingType === 'intermittent' (Nutrition.tsx:471) — there is NO fast-complete / eating-window term in that condition.
- The overlay is a later-sibling absolute inset-0 ... bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm div (Nutrition.tsx:472) with NO pointer-events-none, so it sits on top of NutritionMealList and swallows every tap (eaten checkbox, Skip, Swap, Adjust).
- The completion signal fastDone = elapsed >= FAST_MIN is computed LOCALLY inside FastingBanner (Nutrition.tsx:116) and is never lifted to the page; and backend getFastingStatus returns only {fasting_day, fasting_type} (nutrition.service.ts:107) — no window state — so the overlay condition can never learn the window is open.
- The overlay copy itself promises the opposite: "Your meals unlock when the eating window opens." (en.json nutrition.fasting.window_active_body).

Expected: once the 16h fast completes (banner flips to "Eating window open" / "Your 16-hour fast is complete"), the overlay lifts and meals become tappable so the user can log during their eating window.

Actual: the overlay + blur persist all day; the only way to reveal/log meals is "End fast", which disables fasting tracking for the day entirely.

Repro:
1. /nutrition with a diet plan → tap the "Intermittent" fasting chip → meals blur (expected during the fast).
2. Reach completion — the fast start is back-dated to the last eaten meal (Nutrition.tsx:82-92), so a user whose last meal was >16h ago is already complete; force it with localStorage['nyus_fast_start_<today>'] = String(Date.now() - 17*3600*1000) then reload.
3. Banner ring shows "complete" and text switches to "Eating window open."
4. Tap any meal card → nothing responds; blur/overlay still there. Only "End fast" reveals meals.

Fix: add a fast-complete term to the overlay condition (lift fastDone to the page, or derive it from the fast-start localStorage key) so the overlay only shows while the fast is actually in progress; also add pointer-events-none to the decorative overlay so it never blocks the list when not intended.
issues.reviewReason: STILL FIXED + hardened this tick (app commit e0d44416, pushed to main). Original fix (6275a222) already lifts the 16:8 blur/overlay once the fast completes: FastingBanner publishes fast-complete up via onFastCompleteChange and the meal list overlay only renders while (intermittent && !fastComplete). This tick I closed a 1-frame cosmetic edge — the banner's elapsed started at 0, so on mount it briefly published fastComplete=false before its timer caught up, flashing the overlay for an already-complete fast. Now elapsed is seeded synchronously from the nyus_fast_start_<today> key (mirroring the page seed), so fastDone is correct on first render and no transient false is published. tsc clean; fasting.test.ts + Nutrition.page tests 40/40 green. No faithful full-screen proof possible in the QA env (meal list is hasMeals-gated and this account has no active date-covering diet plan; provisioning prohibited per owner directive). Please verify on-device (start a 16:8 fast, reach completion — overlay lifts, meals tappable, no flash) and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Water intake added on the Nutrition page is silently LOST if the user leaves the page within the 600ms sync-debounce window — the unmount handler cancels the pending write without flushing it.

Component: src/pages/_components/nutrition/useNutritionData.tsx.

What's wrong:
- Adding water updates local state and schedules a debounced backend sync 600ms later: waterSyncTimeout.current = setTimeout(() => { ...upsertDailyLog... }, 600) (:81); rapid taps keep RESETTING that timer (:80).
- The unmount cleanup CANCELS the pending timer without ever flushing the write: clearTimeout(waterSyncTimeout.current); waterSyncTimeout.current = null; (:72-74). No pagehide/visibilitychange/flush path exists.
- The POST is ABSOLUTE, not incremental (water_intake_liters: liters computed from the current ml, :82-85), so the unsynced delta is dropped entirely, not merely delayed.

Expected: water added just before navigating away persists (flush the pending sync on unmount / navigation).

Actual: the pending upsertDailyLog never fires; on return, the water tracker reseeds from the backend's stale value (effect at :57-62) and the added glasses are gone. A burst of taps followed by an immediate tab switch loses the whole unsynced amount.

Repro:
1. /nutrition → tap the add-water control one or more times (watch the count rise).
2. Within ~600ms of the last tap, navigate away (e.g. tap the Dashboard bottom-nav tab — the Nutrition page unmounts).
3. Return to /nutrition → water reads the pre-tap value; the added water was never saved.

Fix: flush the pending sync in the unmount cleanup (fire the upsert immediately, with keepalive, if a timer is pending) instead of just clearing the timeout; or write the final value synchronously before unmount.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED — shipped, awaiting on-device verify. Root cause: adding water schedules a 600ms debounced absolute upsert, but the unmount cleanup CLEARED the pending timer without flushing it, so water added just before navigating away was dropped entirely (the POST is absolute, not incremental). Fix (useNutritionData.tsx, commit 6275a222): a pendingWaterMlRef tracks the latest unsynced value; the unmount cleanup now FLUSHES it (fires the upsert fire-and-forget) instead of discarding, and the debounce clears the ref once it fires. tsc clean. This is a persistence-timing bug with no on-screen state to screenshot, and the water tracker is additionally gated behind hasMeals which this QA account cannot render (no active date-covering diet plan; provisioning prohibited per owner directive). Please verify on-device (tap water, immediately switch tabs, return — count persists) and Resolve.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] In coach chat, marking a planned meal "Eaten" from a meal_plan_card block is silently UN-logged if the block scrolls out of view and back. The card's eaten-state lives only in local component state that resets on virtualized remount, and re-tapping "Mark Eaten" hits a server TOGGLE endpoint that flips the meal back to un-eaten.

Root cause (frontend), src/components/blocks/MealPlanCard.tsx:
- Eaten/skip state is held in local useState(data.meals || []) (line 35), seeded ONCE from the immutable chat-message payload. The component does NOT accept or use cacheKey (unlike the 6 logging blocks, which persist their draft in a module-level Map keyed by cacheKey specifically to survive virtualized remount).
- meal_plan_card is NOT a logging block (src/lib/block-transformers.ts isLoggingBlock set = meal_logger / workout_tracker / daily_checkin / measurement_input / activity_logger / water_logger only). So useBlockSubmit.submitBlock takes the !isLoggingBlock branch (useBlockSubmit.ts:103-107): it calls onChatResponse() and returns WITHOUT ever calling setBlockStatus('completed'). CoachChatMessageList.handleBlockResponse (line 506-517) confirms non-nav non-logging responses never advance blockStatuses.
- So blockStatuses[blockKey] stays unset and status = (blockStatuses[blockKey] ?? block.status ?? 'active') (CoachChatMessageList.tsx:528) stays 'active' forever.

Prod virtualization is ON: FEATURE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE = import.meta.env.VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE === "true" (feature-flags.ts:71) and .env.production line 24 sets VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true. @tanstack/react-virtual windows the message list, so off-screen block rows UNMOUNT and remount on scroll-back. On remount MealPlanCard re-runs useState(data.meals || []) so logged resets to the payload value (false): the "Eaten" badge disappears and the Mark Eaten / Swap / Skip buttons reappear (they only render when !meal.logged && !meal.skipped, line 160).

Backend toggle: handleMarkEaten (line 68-89) guards "if (disabled || meal.logged) return", but after remount meal.logged is false so the guard passes. It calls nutritionService.logMeal({assigned_meal_id}) which POSTs /diet/log-meal, documented "Toggle meal eaten status" (nutrition.service.ts:72), sending NO was_eaten flag, so the server toggles. The meal was already eaten server-side, so this second call flips it to UN-eaten.

Repro (prod build / VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true):
1. Coach sends a "Today's Meals" meal_plan_card. Tap "Mark Eaten" on a meal: optimistic "Eaten" badge, POST /diet/log-meal logs it, buttons vanish.
2. Keep chatting so the block scrolls out of the virtual window, then scroll back.
3. The card re-seeds from the original payload: the "Eaten" badge is gone and Mark Eaten is back.
4. Tap "Mark Eaten" again (natural, it looks un-logged): POST /diet/log-meal toggles the meal back to UN-eaten. The meal is silently dropped from the day's logged totals; no error, no 500.

Expected: a meal logged from the chat card stays logged across scroll; the card reflects server truth on remount.
Actual: the eaten state is discarded on scroll-back and re-tapping un-logs the meal server-side (silent corruption of the nutrition log).

Same root cause (non-logging stateful blocks that ignore cacheKey and are never marked 'completed', so prod virtualization discards local state on remount) also affects grocery_list (checked items visually reset on scroll: GroceryListBlock.tsx:67, block never calls onResponse) and plan_update_proposal (Approve/Modify/Reject re-enable on remount: PlanUpdateBlock local "responded" resets), but MealPlanCard is the data-integrity case.

Fix: persist MealPlanCard's meals (or at least the logged/skipped ids) via cacheKey using a module-level Map + useEffect, exactly like ActivityLoggerBlock / DailyCheckinBlock; OR seed the eaten guard from server truth on mount; OR have the parent mark meal_plan_card 'completed' in blockStatuses once a meal is logged. Also send an explicit was_eaten:true (idempotent) rather than relying on the toggle.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit 0d17e9c2). MealPlanCard silent nutrition-log corruption: eaten/skipped state lived only in local useState seeded from the immutable chat payload and the block never accepted cacheKey, so with prod virtualization ON (VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true) scrolling the block out and back UNMOUNTED it and re-seeded to un-eaten — the Eaten badge vanished, the buttons reappeared, and re-tapping 'Mark Eaten' hit the /diet/log-meal TOGGLE and silently UN-logged the meal. Fix: persist per-block meals via cacheKey (module-level Map + useEffect), exactly like ActivityLoggerBlock/DailyCheckinBlock; cacheKey was already forwarded by InteractiveBlock, the card just ignored it. After remount the Eaten state restores and the buttons stay gone, so the un-log toggle is unreachable. Regression test test/MealPlanCard.test.tsx 'restores a logged meal from cacheKey after unmount/remount' (mark eaten -> unmount -> remount from same payload -> still Eaten, buttons gone, no 2nd toggle call). 27/27 green; tsc clean. Not self-resolving under the pinned-100 bar — please verify on device (mark a chat meal eaten, scroll away and back, confirm it stays Eaten) and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] The in-chat Daily Check-in block DISPLAYS mood (and, when the coach pre-fills defaults, water + sleep) as already set/selected, but submitting without physically re-tapping those controls silently omits them from the log. The mood control also reports aria-checked=true for a value that will not be submitted.

Root cause, src/components/blocks/DailyCheckinBlock.tsx:
- handleSubmit (line 50-60) includes water_ml / sleep_hours / mood ONLY when touched.has(...) is true (weight is gated on weight > 0). The touched set only gains a field when the user physically taps a water preset (line 131), moves the sleep slider (line 158) or taps a mood emoji (line 185).
- But the UI always renders these fields as populated/selected:
  - Mood: const [mood, setMood] = useState(cached?.mood ?? defaults.mood ?? 3) (line 35). With no defaults mood = 3, and the "Okay" emoji renders with the selected ring-2 highlight and aria-checked={mood === m.value} = true (lines 189, 196-197). There is no "nothing selected" state; a chip is ALWAYS shown selected.
  - Sleep: the slider sits at defaults.sleep_hours ?? 7 and the label shows "{sleep}h" (line 152) as if staged.
  - Water: shows "{water} ml" from defaults.water_ml ?? 0 (line 121).

So a user who agrees with the shown mood ("Okay") / water / sleep and taps "Submit Check-in" without re-tapping gets a payload of just {date, weight_kg?}: mood, sleep and water are dropped. It is worst with backend-supplied defaults: the coach's show_daily_checkin can send defaults {water_ml, sleep_hours, mood} (the dev fixture chatBlockFixtures.ts sends water_ml:1800, sleep_hours:7.5, mood:4). The card then displays "1800 ml", a 7.5h slider and a highlighted "Good" mood, but confirming via Submit logs none of them.

The touched gate is deliberate (comment lines 36-37: omit untouched fields, prevents fabricating sleep/mood), but the display contradicts it: the card visually stages values it will not submit, and screen readers announce aria-checked=true on a mood the user never chose and that will not be logged.

Repro:
1. Coach opens a Daily Check-in (no defaults). "Okay" mood shows highlighted/selected (aria-checked true), sleep shows 7h.
2. A user who genuinely feels Okay and slept 7h taps "Submit Check-in" without tapping anything.
3. Payload = {date} only (mood/sleep/water omitted). Mood and sleep are never logged, though the card showed them staged. (With backend defaults populated, the pre-filled water/sleep/mood are likewise dropped on a confirm-only submit.)

Expected: what the card displays as selected/filled is what gets submitted (displayed == submitted).
Actual: mood is always shown selected but omitted unless re-tapped; pre-filled sleep/water defaults are shown but omitted unless re-touched. Silent data loss plus a misleading aria-checked state.

Fix: make displayed state match submitted state. Either (a) include mood/sleep/water when a meaningful value is shown (e.g. include mood/sleep when defaults exist, mirroring weight's value-gate), or (b) render mood with NO chip selected and the sleep slider in an explicit untouched state until the user interacts, so an untouched Submit honestly submits nothing for those fields. Keep aria-checked false until a real selection.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit 0d17e9c2). DailyCheckinBlock displayed==submitted mismatch: the card staged mood/sleep/water (worst with coach-supplied defaults like water 1800/sleep 7.5/mood 'Good') but a confirm-only Submit omitted them because they were gated on a hidden `touched` set; it also rendered aria-checked=true on an unselected mood. Fix: value-gate every field exactly like weight (submit what the card shows) and start mood UNSELECTED (null) so aria-checked is honest and nothing is fabricated; removed the touched machinery. Regression tests test/DailyCheckinBlock.test.tsx: 'does not pre-select or submit a mood when no defaults' + 'submits coach-supplied defaults on confirm-only'. 31/31 green; tsc clean. Not self-resolving under the pinned-100 bar — please confirm on device (open a check-in with backend defaults, tap Submit without re-tapping, verify mood/sleep/water are logged) and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] A rating_scale block whose scale exceeds 10 (max > 10) renders as a Slider, but choosing a value never sends the rating to the coach: the slider freezes after the first movement and onResponse is never called. The dots variant (max <= 10) is fine; only the slider path is broken.

Root cause, src/components/blocks/RatingScaleBlock.tsx:
- disabled = status === "completed" || status === "expired" || value !== null (line 13). It flips to true as soon as local value is non-null.
- Slider (line 81-96): onValueChange={([v]) => { if (!disabled) setValue(v); }} sets value during drag/track-click; onValueCommit={([v]) => { if (disabled) return; ... onResponse({value:v}); }} is the ONLY place the slider calls onResponse.
- onValueChange (pointer move) and onValueCommit (pointer up) are separate pointer events, so React re-renders between them. The first onValueChange sets value, the next render makes disabled === true, the Radix Slider then receives disabled (thumb gets disabled:pointer-events-none per src/components/ui/slider.tsx) and stops tracking the drag, AND onValueCommit's "if (disabled) return" guard now short-circuits. Net: onResponse is effectively UNREACHABLE for the slider. The value shows on screen (line 101-103) but is never sent to the coach, and the thumb sticks at the first position.
- The dots path works because handleSelect (line 17-22) sets value AND calls onResponse atomically in one handler before the disabling re-render.

Repro:
1. Coach sends a rating_scale with max > 10 (e.g. {question, min:0, max:100} or min:1, max:20) so it renders the Slider variant (useDots = max <= 10 is false, line 14).
2. Drag the slider thumb (or tap the track). The thumb freezes at/near the first position and the coach never receives a rating; the interaction is dead after one move.

Expected: dragging/committing the slider sends onResponse({value}) with the chosen number, like the dots variant.
Actual: onResponse never fires for the slider; the rating is silently lost and the control freezes.

Fix: do not derive disabled from value for the slider. Track commit separately, e.g. const [committed, setCommitted] = useState(false); const disabled = status === "completed" || status === "expired" || committed; set committed inside onValueCommit and keep onValueChange only updating value. (The dots path can keep its single-handler behavior.)
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit 0d17e9c2). RatingScaleBlock slider path: root cause was `disabled = ... || value !== null` — the drag (onValueChange) set value, the next render disabled the Radix thumb mid-gesture AND made onValueCommit's `if (disabled) return` short-circuit, so onResponse never fired and the thumb froze after one move. Fix: lock on a separate `committed` flag set only in the commit handler (dots path already commits atomically). Regression test test/RatingScaleBlock.test.tsx 'commits the rating on drag-then-release' asserts onResponse({value:75}) after change+mouseUp (fails on the old code). 82/82 in that file green; tsc clean. Not self-resolving: satisfaction bar is pinned 100, which freezes resolves for your on-device verdict, and this is an interaction deadlock a static screenshot can't show — the proof is the unit test. Please verify a >10-max rating slider commits on device and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Custom workout builder emits non-canonical day_index (can exceed 7) and never re-indexes it, so the backend silently collapses two training days onto the same weekday — one day is duplicated and another weekday is left empty.

Root cause (frontend). In src/pages/onboarding/custom/CustomWorkoutBuilder.tsx:
- nextDayIndex = Math.max(...list.map(d => d.day_index)) + 1 (line ~345) is uncapped (MAX_DAYS/BUILDER_MAX_DAYS = 10, but that only caps the COUNT of tabs, not the index value).
- handleAddDay (line ~350) caps only prev.length, and creates the new day object with NO weekday key.
- handleRemoveDay (line ~362) filters the array but does NOT re-index day_index.
- handleContinue / handleBgContinue (line ~799) emit days.filter(exercises.length>0) VERBATIM with their raw day_index values — no re-index to contiguous 1..N.
- buildDays (line ~145) only sets weekday when the user pre-picked preferred_workout_days; in the default build-it-all flow the intensity screen writes preferred_workout_days: [] (Screen7_5_Intensity.tsx:57), so every seeded day has weekday = undefined.

By contrast CustomDietBuilder.tsx DOES re-index (removeDay maps {...d, day_index: i+1, weekday: WEEKDAYS[i%7]}, and its emit map re-numbers too). The workout builder does neither — this asymmetry is the defect.

Backend (nyu_backend/app/routes/plan_builder_routes.py). _day_index_to_dow (line ~2244) prefers an explicit weekday; with weekday undefined it falls back to _safe_int(day_index, min_v=1, max_v=7) - 1, and _safe_int CLAMPS (min(7, x)). So day_index 7 -> dow 6 (Sunday) and day_index 8 (or 9/10) -> clamp(7) -> dow 6 as well. FitnessWorkoutPlan (db_models.py:1533) has only a NON-unique index on (plan_id, week_number, day_of_week) — no UniqueConstraint — so both rows persist with day_of_week=6. No IntegrityError, no 500: it is a silent duplication.

Reachable in the shipped release flow: FEATURE_DEFER_BUILDERS is OFF in release, so users go straight into the always-custom builders; WorkoutDayTabs surfaces both Add (shown while days.length < 10) and Remove (shown while days.length > 1); openPlanChoice sets plan_build_workout='custom' and the save body sends workout_mode='custom' (the branch that calls _day_index_to_dow).

Repro:
1. Onboarding -> Intensity screen -> pick any non-starter tier (everyday/fit/athlete) -> preferred_workout_days=[]. Workout builder seeds 7 days, day_index 1..7, all weekday undefined.
2. Tap the "x" on Day 4 -> list becomes day_index [1,2,3,5,6,7] (no re-index).
3. Tap "Add day" -> nextDayIndex = max(1,2,3,5,6,7)+1 = 8 -> [1,2,3,5,6,7,8]; the new day has no weekday.
4. Put >=1 exercise on each of the 7 days; tap Continue.
5. save-custom-plan maps 1->0, 2->1, 3->2, 5->4, 6->5, 7->6, and 8 -> clamp(7) -> 6. Two FitnessWorkoutPlan rows land on day_of_week=6 (Sunday); day_of_week=3 (Thursday) gets none.

Expected: every built training day is persisted to its own distinct weekday, contiguous like the diet builder; no day is silently duplicated or dropped.
Actual: 7 distinct built days collapse into 6 weekday slots — a duplicated Sunday and a missing weekday — and the round-trip inversion yields duplicate day_index too.

Fix: in handleContinue/handleBgContinue, re-index before emit: days.filter(d => d.exercises.length > 0).map((d, i) => ({ ...d, day_index: i + 1 })) — mirroring CustomDietBuilder's payload map — and/or re-index in handleRemoveDay/handleAddDay so day_index stays 1..N. Optionally cap the workout builder at 7 days and assign each saved day a distinct weekday.

Note: a weaker "partial preferred-days set" variant (e.g. ["wed"]) was considered and is NOT reachable in the condensed onboarding (Screen7_5_Intensity only ever writes a full week or an empty list), so this issue is specifically about the remove-then-add / add-past-7 path in the default build-all flow.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED (2-layer), frozen at bar=100 pending your on-device verify. Layer 1 (commit c0463e0f): handleContinue/handleBgContinue re-index day_index to contiguous 1..N on emit, killing the remove-then-add gap. Layer 2 (commit 0bb48735, this tick): the builder still allowed up to 10 days while the backend maps each day to a distinct weekday in ONE week (clamps day_index>7 to Sunday), so building 8-10 filled days re-indexed to 8/9/10 still collapsed onto Sunday. Capped BUILDER_MAX_DAYS 10->7 (single cap source for seed/add/coach-reshape), mirroring CustomDietBuilder MAX_DAYS=7; default seed unchanged (full week). Locked by test/onboarding-derive.test.ts cap invariant.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] On the plan-ready overview, the headline "Daily Target" kcal and the macro breakdown are computed from DIFFERENT numbers, so protein·4 + carb·4 + fat·9 does not equal the displayed calorie target.

Root cause (src/pages/onboarding/custom/PlanReadyOverview.tsx). The screen fetches a server-authoritative calorie target and, when present, overrides the local client estimate: displayStats.target = serverCals.target_kcal (line ~105-124; when serverTarget == null it returns calc verbatim, line ~112). The big "Daily Target" number renders {displayStats.target} (line ~308), and BMR / TDEE / deficit / weekly-pace all use displayStats. BUT the macro grid is left on the LOCAL estimate:
- macro grams render calc.proteinG / calc.carbG / calc.fatG (line ~320-322)
- macroCals = [calc.proteinG*4, calc.carbG*4, calc.fatG*9] (line ~226-229)
- the "%" denominator = calc.proteinG*4 + calc.carbG*4 + calc.fatG*9 (line ~327) — i.e. calc.target, NOT displayStats.target
- bar widths derive from macroCals (calc.*) too (line ~230-231, 331)

And calc.carbG is the balancing macro filled to calc.target: onboarding-calc.ts:135 carbG = round((target - proteinG*4 - fatG*9)/4) (protein/fat are weight-based and target-independent). So the entire macro sub-card sums to calc.target while the headline shows displayStats.target.

The divergence is the designed steady state, not a rare edge: the server two-axis target and the client flat-multiplier estimate are DIFFERENT algorithms (documented in-repo at useDisplayStats.ts and other.service.ts, added for QA i-20260618-9d43 precisely because the client estimate "overshot" the server plan). Whenever the server target has loaded (the common case on this screen) it differs from calc.target by tens-to-hundreds of kcal.

Repro: user current_weight_kg=80, goal=lose. proteinG=160, fatG=80. Say client calc.target=1700 -> carbG=round((1700-640-720)/4)=85; macro kcal = [640,340,720] sum = 1700. Server two-axis target_kcal=2000 -> displayStats.target=2000. Rendered: headline "2000 kcal/day", but the macro grid shows 160g/85g/80g summing to 1700 kcal, with percentages (38/20/42) taken over 1700. A data-literate athlete checking 32% of 2000 vs the printed grams finds they are ~300 kcal short and do not reconcile.

Expected: the macro grams (carbs especially) and the %/bars are derived from the same target shown in the headline, so P·4 + C·4 + F·9 == the displayed kcal.
Actual: headline uses the server target while macros use the client estimate — the sum of the parts != the stated total.

Why it is the outlier / not intentional: the sibling PostPlanTour.tsx derives BOTH its headline (calc.target) AND its macros (calc.*) from the SAME calc object, so it is internally consistent. PlanReadyOverview is the only screen mixing a server-sourced headline with client-sourced macros — an incomplete retrofit of the 9d43 fix (headline/deficit/tdee/bmr/weeklyChange were realigned to the server target, the macro grid was left on calc). No test covers this (there is no PlanReadyOverview test).

Fix: recompute the macro grams against displayStats.target — e.g. carbG = round((displayStats.target - proteinG*4 - fatG*9)/4) — and base macroCals / percentages / bar widths on displayStats.target. Note: simply swapping the grid to read displayStats.* is NOT enough, because displayStats spreads ...calc and only overrides target/bmr/tdee/energyDelta/deficit/weeklyChange — displayStats.carbG === calc.carbG — so carbG must be rebalanced.

This is distinct from i-20260706-9b3c (imperial kg vs lbs display) — it is a calorie/macro reconciliation bug, unit-agnostic.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit c0463e0f). PlanReadyOverview macro grid now rebalances carbs against displayStats.target (the same server-authoritative number the headline shows), and macroCals / % / bar widths all derive from it — so P4+C4+F9 == the displayed kcal. Before, the grid stayed on the client calc estimate (summing to calc.target) while the headline used the server target, diverging by tens-to-hundreds of kcal. Regression lock: test/qa-i20260710-fixes.test.ts (reconciliation invariant, proves old grid would NOT reconcile) — green; tsc clean. Not auto-resolving: bar pinned 100. PlanReadyOverview is onboarding-internal (no standalone route to headlessly capture the live server-target state), so the attached proof is a faithful before/after render of the macro card math (2000 kcal: old carbs 85g -> sum 1700 != 2000; fixed carbs 160g -> sum 2000). Verify in a fresh onboarding on device and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] The "infinite" meal-idea swiper permanently stops topping up its deck after the first background fetch that is interrupted by a swipe — the deck is silently capped at the initial ~20 cards for the rest of the session (and across every re-open).

Root cause (src/components/plan-builder/MealSuggestionSwiper.tsx). The background top-up uses a single-flight mutex ref, but releases it conditionally:
- fetchingMoreRef = useRef(false) (line ~78) — persists across renders. Only reset in ONE place.
- Top-up effect: guard "if (fetchingMoreRef.current) return;" (line ~129), then fetchingMoreRef.current = true (line ~133), starts a force:true (cache-bypassing, live-LLM, ~14s) suggestMealCached fetch (line ~136).
- The reset is gated on !cancelled: .finally(() => { if (!cancelled) fetchingMoreRef.current = false; }) (line ~147).
- The effect cleanup sets cancelled = true (line ~149-151). Effect deps include index (line ~153), so the very next swipe (skip() -> setIndex(i+1), line ~189) re-runs the effect and fires the previous closure's cleanup -> cancelled = true.
- When the in-flight fetch then settles, .then early-returns on cancelled (line ~138) AND .finally skips the reset because !cancelled is false -> fetchingMoreRef.current is now stuck true FOREVER. Every subsequent top-up early-returns at line 129.

Nothing else clears the ref: the open/re-open effect (line ~88-117) resets loading/error/cards/index but NOT fetchingMoreRef; and the component only "return null"s when closed (line ~220) — it never unmounts, because the caller renders it as {suggestMeal && <MealSuggestionSwiper open=... />} and suggestMeal stays defined once set (setSuggestTarget is only ever called with a non-null value, never reset). So the stuck ref survives close/reopen for the whole builder session; even "More ideas" (reloadKey) fetches a fresh 20 but that deck is capped at 20 too.

Because force:true hits the live LLM (~14s) and the user reached index 10 by actively swiping (seconds per card), the interrupting swipe is the DEFAULT, not the exception — the fetch is almost always orphaned.

Repro:
1. Onboarding -> custom diet builder -> tap "Suggest" on a meal. Swiper loads 20 cards, index 0.
2. Swipe/x down to index 10 -> top-up condition (cards.length - index = 10) fires -> fetchingMoreRef=true, ~14s fetch starts.
3. Swipe once more before it resolves -> setIndex(11) -> cleanup sets cancelled=true; effect re-runs and early-returns at the guard (no new fetch registered).
4. Fetch resolves: results discarded (cancelled), and the .finally skips the reset -> fetchingMoreRef stuck true.
5. From now on no top-up ever runs. At index 20 the UI degrades to the manual "That's all the ideas / More ideas" gate — the exact fallback the infinite-deck feature (QA i-20260623-ab17) was built to eliminate. Reopening the swiper for the same or a different meal also never tops up.

Expected: as the user nears the end of the queue a fresh batch is always fetched and appended, keeping the deck endless across the session and across re-opens.
Actual: the deck freezes at ~20 cards after the first interrupted top-up and never grows again.

Fix: release the mutex unconditionally — drop the !cancelled guard on line ~147 so .finally always does fetchingMoreRef.current = false (safe, because the guard at line 129 already prevents a second concurrent fetch, so only one .finally is ever pending). For defense in depth also clear fetchingMoreRef.current = false in the open effect (line ~88-117).

Distinct from i-20260706-4ea7 (which is about the per-meal Suggest context omitting saved mealPrefs / cold vs warmed deck) — this is a separate ref-release deadlock in the top-up path.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit c0463e0f). MealSuggestionSwiper top-up mutex now releases unconditionally in .finally (was gated on !cancelled, so a swipe mid-fetch left fetchingMoreRef stuck true forever and froze the infinite deck at ~20 cards) + it resets on every open/reload. Regression lock: test/qa-i20260710-fixes.test.ts (mutex-release invariant incl. old-behavior-fails assertion) — 7/7 green; tsc clean. Not auto-resolving: satisfaction bar is pinned 100 (freezes resolves for your on-device verdict) and I won't self-score 100 because the fix screenshot (the /customize/diet builder surface) can't visually show a time/interaction deadlock — the proof is the unit test. Please verify on device (swipe ~10 meals fast, confirm the deck keeps topping up) and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Daily "N-Day Streak Bonus" reward is off by one day and always shows 0 XP, because it double-counts the day increment.

Root cause (backend app/services/daily_report.py). generate_daily_report runs Step 2 _evaluate_streak BEFORE Step 3 _evaluate_daily_rewards on the SAME plan object. On a maintained day _evaluate_streak already does plan.current_streak = (plan.current_streak or 0) + 1 (daily_report.py:407; the full/vrat fasting branch does the same at :339). Then _evaluate_daily_rewards reads that ALREADY-incremented value and adds +1 again: streak = (plan.current_streak or 0) + (1 if len(rewards) > 0 else 0); if streak in (7,14,21,30,60,90): append streak_bonus (daily_report.py:503-505). The +1 was written as if current_streak still reflected yesterday, but Step 2 has made it today, so it over-counts by one.

Demonstrable symptoms (assume a maintained day earns >=1 other reward, so the +1 fires):
(A) OFF BY ONE DAY. On the 6th consecutive maintained day Step 2 sets current_streak=6, then Step 3 computes streak=6+1=7 and mints a DailyReward reward_type=streak_bonus labelled "7-Day Streak Bonus" on reward_date = day 6. On the true 7th day current_streak=7 -> streak=7+1=8, NOT in (7,14,21,30,60,90), so NO streak bonus is minted on the actual milestone day. Every milestone bonus fires one day early (6/13/20/29/59/89) and never on the real mark.
(B) DISPLAYED XP STUCK AT 0. streak_bonus reconciles via REWARD_LEDGER_SOURCES -> streak_milestone_7/30/90 (daily_report.py:562). But the streak_milestone_7 XPLedger row is only minted by _evaluate_streak on the day current_streak==7 (day 7). On day 6 (when the reward row exists) no such ledger row exists yet, so _reconcile_reward_xp credits 0 -> the reward row xp_earned stays 0. On day 7 the milestone XP is minted but there is no streak_bonus reward row that day to display it. Display != credit for this reward.
(C) NON-MAINTAINED EDGE. If today is NOT maintained (day_score < 0.75, current_streak not incremented / reset) but the user still earned >=1 reward, streak = yesterday_streak + 1 can still land on a milestone value and mint a streak bonus on a day the streak was not actually maintained.

Repro: log a clean, streak-maintaining day for 6 consecutive days on an active plan; the nightly daily report (or GET /reports/daily generating the day-6 report) creates a DailyReward streak_bonus "7-Day Streak Bonus" dated day 6 with xp_earned 0, and day 7 gets none. Surfaces on the dashboard reward reveal (RewardRevealSheet).

Expected: the N-day streak bonus is minted on the day the streak actually reaches N (current_streak == N), and its reconciled XP matches the streak_milestone_N ledger row minted the same night.

Fix: in _evaluate_daily_rewards drop the extra +1 and read the streak Step 2 already computed, e.g. streak = (plan.current_streak or 0); (optionally gate on streak_maintained so a non-maintained day never mints a streak bonus). That aligns the reward day with the milestone day AND lets _reconcile_reward_xp find the same-night streak_milestone_N ledger row so display == credit.
issues.reviewReason:
FIXED + DEPLOYED to prod (140.245.238.38, backend healthy) — commit 547f631. Root cause exactly as you diagnosed: _evaluate_streak (Step 2) already increments plan.current_streak for the day, then _evaluate_daily_rewards (Step 3) did `streak = current_streak + (1 if rewards else 0)` and re-added the day. issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Onboarding: the "Weekly pace" the plan-ready screens promise can be ~2x what the diet the app actually built delivers. Two different formulas feed the same "Weekly pace kg/week" label. PostPlanTour (the screen every user sees on the happy path) shows calc.weeklyChange from calcOnboardingStats (src/lib/onboarding-calc.ts:104-118), which is DATE-DRIVEN: goal_delta / weeks_to_target (weights win over calorie math). PlanReadyOverview (the failure/retry-only surface, src/pages/onboarding/custom/PlanReadyOverview.tsx:110-124,338-347) OVERRIDES that with a CALORIE-DERIVED rate off the server target: (serverTarget - tdee) * 7 / 7700. When the requested timeline needs a faster loss than the safe deficit cap allows, these diverge and BOTH the tour + overview under/over-report vs reality. Worked example (female 80kg->65kg / 165cm / 30y, 120-day plan, activity_level blank -> 1.55 mult): BMR 1520, TDEE 2356, deficit capped at min(500, tdee-bmr)=500 -> target 1856 kcal. Date-driven pace = 15kg / 17.1wk = 0.88 kg/wk (shown on PostPlanTour). Calorie-derived pace = 500*7/7700 = 0.45 kg/wk (shown on PlanReadyOverview + what the 1856-kcal plan actually delivers). So the tour promises 0.88 kg/wk (goal hit in the chosen 17 wk) while the built plan only supports 0.45 kg/wk (goal really ~33 wk out). The pace gate on Screen4 only fires 'caution' here (1.09%/wk bodyweight = acknowledge-and-continue), so it does NOT block this case. Repro: onboard with an aggressive-but-acknowledgeable timeline, finish, read Weekly pace on the tour; force a save/finalize failure to also see PlanReadyOverview and compare. Two questions for owner (product call -> filing, not auto-fixing): (1) which number is the honest "Weekly pace" - the achievable calorie-derived rate, or the required-to-hit-date rate? (2) whichever we pick, PostPlanTour + PlanReadyOverview should show the SAME one. Note: happy path only shows PostPlanTour, so impact is the over-promise, not a side-by-side mismatch.

fix.description: Owner ruling applied (reviewReply 'achievable calorie-derived rate'). calcOnboardingStats now returns achievableWeeklyChange = the calorie-derived pace (daily energy delta) captured BEFORE the date-driven override; PostPlanTour's Weekly-pace label reads it (src/pages/onboarding/PostPlanTour.tsx:261), matching PlanReadyOverview which already derives pace the same way. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player declares a set the "final set" based purely on set NUMBER, not on whether all target sets were actually logged. In ExerciseWheelPicker.handleLogSet (src/components/ExerciseWheelPicker.tsx:341) it fires onSetComplete(true) whenever setData.set_number === targetSets, with no check that sets 1..targetSets-1 were logged. Activity.handleSetComplete (src/pages/Activity.tsx:672) then advances to the next exercise or declares the whole workout done. Two demonstrable symptoms from the same root cause:

(A) OUT-OF-ORDER LOG -> premature completion. Repro: open an exercise whose target is 3 sets (e.g. 3x8-10), tap the Set 3 row to activate it, and log it FIRST (reverse-pyramid / top-set-first is common for the strength persona this app targets). Expected: nothing special; sets 1-2 still pending. Actual: onSetComplete(true) fires -> if more exercises remain, the "Set complete - Next up" banner pops prompting the user to move on; if this is the last exercise, "Workout complete" + confetti + completion sound fire with only 1 of 3 sets logged.

(B) EDIT-AFTER-COMPLETE -> celebration replays. Repro: log all 3 sets of the LAST exercise normally (workout-complete banner shows, confetti + sound fire once - correct). The picker stays mounted/open above the banner. Tap the already-logged Set 3 row -> the editor expands -> tap "Update". Expected: a silent value update. Actual: handleLogSet runs again with set_number === targetSets -> onSetComplete(true) -> Activity.handleSetComplete else-branch unconditionally re-runs setShowWorkoutCelebration(true) + playCompleteCue(), so the confetti overlay and completion sound REPLAY on every edit of the final set.

Fix: gate completion on distinct logged target sets covering 1..target_sets (count reached), not on set_number equality; and skip re-firing the celebration when showWorkoutComplete is already true.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Profile: an edited display name silently reverts to the stale server name after the user navigates away from /profile and back. The "edited-name-wins" override only survives while Profile stays mounted.

Root cause (frontend), src/pages/Profile.tsx:
- preferredName = editedName ?? profileName (line 106). editedName is component useState(null) (line 94), set ONLY by the mount effect at lines 95-104 that compares the live user.name against a per-mount nameBaseline useRef (line 93).
- On remount (route change away + back), the useRef re-initialises to {set:false} and editedName resets to null. The effect first run takes the "!nameBaseline.current.set" branch: it captures the CURRENT user.name as the new baseline and returns WITHOUT setting editedName. So a name the user already edited (now persisted in user.name) is treated as the baseline, not an edit, and editedName stays null.
- profileName comes from the ["profile-basic-info"] query (staleTime 5 min, lines 77-82). The edit is never written back to that endpoint (POST /users/me name save is a documented TODO(backend); ProfileEditNameSheet only optimistically updates AuthContext user.name + localStorage via updateUser). So profileName is still the old onboarding name.
- Result: preferredName = null ?? "das" = "das". ProfileIdentityCard.getDisplayName() returns preferredName first (ProfileIdentityCard.tsx:80-86), so the persisted edited user.name is never shown.

Repro (QA acct "das"):
1. /profile -> tap the pencil -> edit name to "Bob" -> save. Display shows "Bob" (context + localStorage now hold "Bob").
2. Navigate to /dashboard, then back to /profile.
3. Display reverts to "das". Reopening the edit sheet seeds "das" (Profile.tsx:181 initialName={preferredName ?? user?.name ...}). The edit appears lost.

Expected: an edited name persists across navigation for the session (matching the sheet own promise) until the backend save endpoint lands.
Actual: it reverts on remount; only survives if the user never leaves Profile.

Fix (note the trap): do NOT naively use "user.name ?? profileName" for preferredName -- for a user who never edited, user.name can be the generated username while profileName is the real onboarding name (see the conflicting notes at Profile.tsx:71-76 vs ProfileIdentityCard.tsx:26-28), so precedence-reshuffling risks REGRESSING to the generated username. Safer: (a) invalidate/refetch ["profile-basic-info"] after a successful in-session name save so profileName itself updates, or (b) persist editedName outside component state (module Map / context / localStorage flag) so the override survives remount. Confirm which of user.name / profileName actually holds the generated username on this build before choosing.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Profile: avatar upload will silently drop the image file (sends empty JSON {"file":{}} instead of multipart form-data). This is a REGRESSION of the fix for i-20260704-a0ec, which over-corrected.

Root cause (frontend):
- The shared axios instance is created with an instance-level default header Content-Type: application/json (src/lib/api-client.ts:12-13).
- The avatar upload (src/pages/_components/profile/ProfileIdentityCard.tsx:130-132) builds a FormData, appends "file", and does apiClient.post("/users/me/avatar", formData) with NO per-request Content-Type override.
- Commit 98386822 (i-20260704-a0ec) REMOVED the previous "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" override, reasoning "let axios set it automatically." But that only works when there is no instance default forcing JSON. Because the instance default is application/json, axios 1.x transformRequest (node_modules/axios/lib/defaults/index.js) sees a JSON content-type on a FormData body and runs formDataToJSON -> serializes it to the string {"file":{}} and sends Content-Type: application/json. Verified by running the repo axios with the identical instance config: body = {"file":{}}, no multipart, no boundary, binary gone.

Why latent today: the backend /users/me/avatar endpoint does not exist yet (404s) and the catch masks it as a "Photo saved locally" toast. So no current user impact -- but the moment the backend avatar endpoint ships, uploads will fail server-side (empty JSON, no file) with no error surfaced to the user.

Correct fix: neither the removed "multipart/form-data" (breaks because axios/XHR will not append the boundary when you set the header manually -- the original i-20260704-a0ec concern) NOR the current bare post (JSON default). Set the per-request header to undefined so axios deletes the JSON default and the browser generates "multipart/form-data; boundary=...":
  apiClient.post("/users/me/avatar", formData, { headers: { "Content-Type": undefined } })
Ship this together with the backend endpoint so it can be verified end-to-end. Same pattern would bite any future FormData upload on this instance (e.g. ProgressPhotos, support attachments) -- audit those when fixing.
